text:
Mira: heads-up — large model-serving streams between pods in us-west-2a -> us-west-2b are intermittently stalling during KV-cache syncs. Sidecars report HTTP/2 stream resets and we see stalled token delivery in traces. :eyes:

Ash: any packet loss or retries on the wire? Which nodes/pods are hit?

Mira: hitting gpu-12/gpu-13 pair and a few others. Top-level symptoms: long tail latency spikes, client shows "STREAM_RESET" and the server sidecar logs 'send buffer full, no progress'. No pod OOM.

Ram: could be segmentation/MTU related with VXLAN encapsulation. When large token batches go over the path they get sliced and trigger odd TCP/H2 behavior. Can you paste output of ip route / ip link from a pair?

Mira: here are quick results from gpu-12 -> gpu-13:
```
$ ip link show dev eth0
3: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
$ ip -d link show vxlan0
34: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default
$ ip route get 10.21.34.56
10.21.34.56 via 10.0.0.1 dev vxlan0 src 10.0.1.12 uid 1000 cache mtu 1450
```

Mira: note: pod network MTU 1500, overlay (vxlan) is 1450 — packets larger than 1450 get fragmented.

Ash: that MTU mismatch is suspicious. Does ethtool show offloads enabled? GRO/GSO can hide fragmentation until the NIC, then it explodes.

Mira: ethtool -k eth0 shows gso, gro, tso all on.

Ram: try disabling GRO/GSO on the host for a quick repro. We had similar stream hangs where HTTP/2 windowing + fragmented frames caused the sidecar to stall waiting for flow-control acks. Command:
```
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
```

Olivia: also check if PMTU discovery is getting blocked. If ICMP is filtered between AZs the DF bit leads to silent fragmentation or drops. sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 can help while we diagnose.

Mira: ran that probe switch and saw more consistent stalls go away for ~30m. Setting it back to 0 the issue returns.

infra-bot: NetworkPathMonitor: path-mtu reduced to 1400 on node gpu-12 (detected 2026-11-04T10:21:30Z).

Ash: gpu-12's vxlan MTU 1450 -> path MTU 1400, weird. Maybe an edge router clamping to 1400 due to encap + cloud provider tunnel. We should avoid host-wide disable long term but can roll a targeted mitigation.

Ram: long-term fix options: 1) normalize overlay MTU to account for maximum encaps overhead (set vxlan mtu = host_mtu - encap_overhead), 2) enable PMTU discovery reliably (allow ICMP/TIME_EXCEEDED across AZs), 3) disable offloads at host or in sidecar's interface when streaming large frames, 4) force gRPC to use smaller initial window/frame sizes for KV syncs.

Olivia: for immediate mitigation I suggest a daemonset that sets vxlan0 mtu to 1400 on affected nodes and a sidecar config change to cap max frame chunk to 1200 bytes. We'll test canary on two nodes.

Mira: working on daemonset manifest (privileged initContainer) — snippet: 
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: overlay-mtu-fix
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      hostNetwork: true
      containers:
      - name: set-mtu
        image: busybox
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1400 || true"]
```

Ash: put a node selector for gpu nodes and limit to us-west-2 for the canary. Also include a probe to check sidecar logs after patch.

Mira: deployed canary to gpu-12,gpu-13 with selector. Early telemetry: stalls dropped 90% on those nodes, stream resets disappeared in the patched pods. :thumbsup:

Olivia: follow-up: we'll open a ticket with the cloud provider to understand why encap path MTU is 1400 (VXLAN + provider tunnel). Also add egress rules to allow ICMP for PMTU.

Ram: assign owners & next steps?

Mira: owners: Mira -> immediate canary/rollout, Ash -> monitoring/probes, Olivia -> provider ticket + security/ICMP change, Ram -> long-term sidecar gRPC frame sizing change. I'll post results in #incidents if the rollouts go clean.

Ash: thx. If anyone sees re-appearance, do not restart pods — rotate nodes after daemonset applied to avoid transient re-introducing old MTU.

Mira: noted. Will coordinate with oncall. Closing this thread for now, will update with provider response. :white_check_mark:
